title: Ex vivo Identification of Specific Gene Vector Capsids for Tumor-targeted Gene Therapy with Adeno-associated Viral Vectors
summary:
Establishing novel treatment paradigms in cancer is urgently needed. Gene therapy has great potential in the field of cancer therapy, however, previous methods in the course of inserting viral vectors ("gene shuttles") are neither sufficiently effective nor sufficiently specific to allow treatment upon systemic administration in human patients.
The aim of this study is to isolate novel capsids from random AAV peptide libraries that allow efficient and selective tumor transduction after intravascular administration in the human setting. 
Patients included in this study will donate a portion of their tumor tissue that is not required by the pathologist for diagnostic tissue examination after surgical tumor removal. Patients with previously untreated renal cell or colon cancer will be included. Donated tissue is processed in the laboratory. AAV peptide banks (a large variety of different gene vectors, only a tiny, previously unknown fraction of which are suitable for gene delivery into tumor tissue) are injected through the arteries of the surgical specimen after surgical removal. DNA is then isolated and amplified from the AAV particles, which were able to introduce genetic material into the tumor tissue using their special properties. These are used to produce AAV gene vectors specifically targeted to the tumor.
Patients will not come into contact with AAV particles or other research agents at any time during this study. Diagnostic testing will not be delayed or compromised in quality or quantity as a result of this study. It is anticipated that this study will be an important step in establishing the use of targeted gene vectors following systemic administration in human tumor patients.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of kidney, except renal pelvis

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
previously untreated colon cancer or renal cell cancer with indication for hemicolectomy or nephrectomy, respectively; size of the tumor to be resected ≥ 2 cm; ability to understand the protocol and give informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
medical or psychological impairments or legal restrictions resulting in reduced capability to give informed consent; lack of any of the listed inclusion criteria; if histopathological workup after the library perfusion will unexpectedly yield a diagnosis other than the expected colon or renal cell cancer, respectively, the patient will be excluded from the trial
